defect_interactions.interaction_type: particle shear (dislocation glide across κ-carbide shear planes)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Strengthening contribution of the κ-carbides is described by a particle shear model (σ_shear = α f^1/2 d_Car^1/2) rather than an Orowan mechanism; shear deformation also facilitates the glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes, resulting in weakened work hardening. The paper's fit gives a slope of 97.1 MPa/nm^1/2 for yield strength versus d_Car^0.5 and states shear strengthening is still active for κ-carbide sizes as large as 50 nm.

interfaces.interface_notes: Small amounts of ferrite (3.30 vol% in the 20%Mn steel) are present in addition to the austenite/K-carbide interfaces; the austenite grain size is refined by the ferrite phase. No intergranular κ-carbides are reported for this sample.
interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides precipitate from spinodal decomposition and ordering of C and Al in the austenite phase during the 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment; their size in the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series decreases with increasing Mn content (18 nm at 20%Mn, 5 nm at 25%Mn, 3 nm at 30%Mn, 2 nm at 35%Mn).

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent (the κ-carbides assume a coherent interface with the austenite matrix as evidenced by the SAED observations); orientation relationship reported for the κ/γ couple in this paper is (001)κ || (001)γ

interfaces.slip_behavior: The κ-carbides are sheared by gliding dislocations (particle shear model) rather than bypassed by Orowan looping; this shear deformation lowers the work hardening rate as the κ-carbide size increases. The 20%Mn steel has the largest κ-carbides (18 nm) of the Mn series and correspondingly the lowest work hardening rate of that series.

processing_steps.method: high-frequency vacuum induction melting (50 kg capacity) followed by casting into an ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm; applied to all designed Fe-Mn-Al-C compositions.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm and then air-cooled to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled rods were solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this is the final state of the sample (process_id proc_st-1050c-2h-wq).

elongation.direction: tensile axis parallel to rod axis
tensile axis parallel to rod axis

strain_hardening_rate.note: The work hardening rate increases with increasing Mn content; within the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series the 20%Mn steel shows the lowest work hardening rate (Fig. 8(b): the black 20Mn dashed curve is the lowest), and the paper states the 30%Mn steel shows a monotonic decrease of work hardening rate.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Room-temperature engineering stress-strain curve of the 20%Mn steel (Fe(x)Mn11Al1C, 1050 °C/2 h + WQ) presented in Fig. 2(b) together with the other Mn contents.

stress_strain_distribution.type: maximum true stress σ_TS just before necking (crack nucleation)

ultimate_tensile_strength.direction: tensile axis parallel to rod axis

yield_strength.direction: tensile axis parallel to rod axis

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS tensile machine; two solution-treated specimens tested and the reported data are the average value of two specimens; stress-strain jumps after yielding caused by extensometer removal do not affect the measurements
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm and diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to the rod axis, cut from water-quenched rods (Fig. 1(a))

defects.type: Σ3 annealing twin boundaries, twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 47.8% (Table 3); the text reports ~62% for this sample

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed austenite grains with abundant Σ3 annealing twin boundaries

precipitates.coherency: coherent interface with the austenite matrix (evidenced by SAED)
precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed within the austenite matrix
precipitates.type: κ-carbide (L'12-type perovskite carbide precipitated in austenite from spinodal decomposition/ordering of C and Al)

phases_present.morphology: green BCC phase patches/bands within the austenite matrix

microstructure_list.region: scattered patches and along a band (EBSD map of the 20%Mn steel)

structures.number_of_phases: 2 major phases (FCC austenite + BCC ferrite) plus κ-carbide precipitates
structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h + water quenching the Mn-20 (Fe19.09Mn10.87Al1.01C) steel consists of an austenite (FCC) matrix with a small amount of retained ferrite (BCC, 3.30 vol%) and fine κ-carbides (~18 nm) uniformly distributed in the austenite; the small ferrite fraction refines the austenite grain size to about 9.9 μm.
